prompt:
A desktop landing page for sqwer, a free touch-typing course for beginners and schools, rendered edge to edge as a finished website screen with crisp readable text, no browser window, no device, no desk.

The page is built like a brick build-instruction booklet: pale sky-blue instruction pages as the ground, black keyline drawings, oversized step numerals that do most of the teaching, wordless arrows, a cornered 1:1 call-out box, everything aligned to a strict grid module. It must look precise and grown-up, for adults and schools, not a toy.

What leads: Step 1 of 125. A large keyline drawing of a computer keyboard in perspective, every key already learned shown ghosted in pale grey, and the two new keys F and J arriving bright ultramarine along dashed arrows onto their seats. A 1:1 call-out box in the corner shows the two keycaps F and J with their small bumps. Next to the giant numeral "1", the line "Learn to type properly, one key at a time." and a caption "Your first two keys. 4 minutes." One clear ultramarine button: "Get started". Below, the next steps begin: "2  D and K", "3  S and L", each a small ghosted keyboard with its new keys bright.

Frame: the sqwer wordmark top left, navigation "Learn  Practice  Ranked", "Sign in" at the far right. Clean grotesk labels, an elegant serif for the main line.
note: Free-plan output carries an OpenArt watermark; small text is garbled by the model.
